label: TP
reason: User-supplied parameter flows directly to the cookie value via split(' ')[0] which preserves HTML entities and special characters. The cookie is added to the response with Secure and HttpOnly flags, but these mitigate clickjacking and MIME-type confusion, not XSS within the cookie attribute itself. Since the cookie value is reflected in the HTTP response header (Set-Cookie), script tags injected by the user remain executable in the browser context.

evidence.note: User parameter extracted from request and passed to doSomething
doSomething splits input preserving potentially malicious content
Cookie created with unencoded user value and written to response
